summary: Verified the Plume chat tool-call JSON leak fix end-to-end. All 8 pytest cases pass on /api/astrology/v3/chat (admin authenticated) and /api/plume-chat (anonymous fallback). Frontend /consultation (ChatIA page) tested with the admin account for 2 prompts — replies are rich French markdown ending with open questions, no JSON leak. Health barrier is respected on both endpoints.

issues: React warning in console: shorthand vs non-shorthand style property mix on padding/paddingTop — cosmetic only, no functional impact

action_items: Note: The request mentioned route /chat-ia but no such route exists. ChatIA component is mounted at /consultation and /chat-astral. If the customer expects a /chat-ia URL, main agent may want to add an alias Route in App.js.
Minor: React console warning about mixing padding shorthand and paddingTop — can be cleaned up in ChatIA.js styles (non-blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: Backend guard is robust: _is_tool_leak() uses a strict regex + json.loads verification and refuses only true tool-call JSON. Text starting with '{' but not fully parseable as a dict with 'action'/'action_input' will not be flagged as a leak, which is the correct behaviour.

The v3/chat endpoint pre-embeds the natal chart in the system prompt AND sends disable_tools=True to astro_chat(), which removes 'enabled_tools' from the payload sent to astrology.io — that is the correct fix for the remote server leaking tool calls in message content.

There is one duplicated PLUME system prompt (PLUME_SYSTEM_PROMPT in routes/astrology_v3.py and SYSTEM_PROMPT_PLUME in services/plume_chat.py). They are almost identical but must be kept in sync manually. Consider extracting to a single constant to avoid drift.

In services/plume_chat.py the pre-loaded history is replayed by sending each past user message via chat.send_message() *before* the new one. Each of those calls hits the LLM and drops the assistant responses — this doubles latency & cost on multi-turn sessions and can lead to context divergence. Consider passing history to LlmChat directly instead of iterating.
Session_id derived from user_id[:8] in v3 chat (f'plume-{user_id[:8]}') could collide across users if two IDs share the first 8 chars. Low probability but easy to salt with a random suffix.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (2/2 prompts rendered clean French text — no JSON leak, open questions present)

test_credentials: Admin: admin@plume-astrale.fr / PlumeAdmin2026 (login OK, birth_data set to 15/05/1990 12:00 Paris via PUT /api/auth/profile)
seed_data_creation: Fixture ensure_birth_data (autouse=True) updates admin profile with birth_date=1990-05-15, birth_time=12:00, birth_place=Paris, lat=48.8566, lon=2.3522 to guarantee v3/chat has all data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix confirmed working. Backend endpoint /api/astrology/v3/chat correctly pre-embeds natal chart, calls astro_chat with disable_tools=True, and retries once with anti-JSON reminder if a leak still occurs (belt-and-suspenders). /api/plume-chat has the same guard. Frontend ChatIA (/consultation) has isToolLeak() guard + LEAK_FALLBACK string as belt-3rd-suspenders. IMPORTANT: the route /chat-ia mentioned in the review does NOT exist — actual routes are /consultation and /chat-astral. LLM used for /plume-chat is currently gpt-4o-mini (services/plume_chat.py line 176), not GPT-5.4 as the module docstring claims — may want to align comment with reality.
rca of the issue: Root cause: astrology.io's /chat/completions endpoint, when called with 'enabled_tools' in the payload, was streaming back the raw tool-call JSON ({"action":"astrology.get_chart", "action_input":{...}}) as the plain message content instead of running the tool loop server-side. That JSON was then stored as the assistant reply and rendered as-is in the UI. Mitigation applied: (1) pre-compute the natal chart via aio.natal_chart() and inject it into the system prompt before the LLM call, (2) call astro_chat(..., disable_tools=True) which omits the 'enabled_tools' key entirely from the request payload, (3) if a leak still slips through, retry once with an explicit anti-JSON reminder, (4) if the retry still leaks, return a friendly French fallback, (5) mirror the guard on the frontend (isToolLeak + LEAK_FALLBACK) so even a bad past response in cache is replaced. All layers verified working via backend pytest + Playwright UI test.
